questions.q: What three things are mandatory when defining a model by subclassing nn.Module?
options: Import numpy, define __init__, define __len__
Subclass nn.Module, call super().__init__() in __init__, and implement forward()
Define __getitem__, __len__, and __call__
Call torch.compile, set requires_grad, and define backward()
questions.explain: Every nn.Module subclass must call super().__init__() before assigning any parameters or submodules, and must implement forward() to define its computation.

questions.q: What does wrapping a tensor in nn.Parameter accomplish?
options: It moves the tensor to the GPU automatically
It sets requires_grad=True and, once assigned as a module attribute, causes nn.Module to automatically register and track it as a learnable parameter
It converts the tensor to a NumPy array
It freezes the tensor so it can never be updated
questions.explain: nn.Parameter is a tensor subclass that enables gradient tracking and signals to nn.Module's attribute-scanning mechanism that this tensor should be included in .parameters().

questions.q: Why should you call model(x) instead of model.forward(x) directly?
options: model.forward(x) is slower to execute
model(x) invokes nn.Module's __call__, which runs registered hooks and other bookkeeping before/after forward(); calling .forward() directly bypasses that machinery
model.forward(x) only works on CPU tensors
There is no difference between the two
questions.explain: nn.Module implements __call__ to handle hooks and other internal logic around the forward pass. Calling model(x) goes through __call__; calling .forward(x) directly skips it, which can cause subtle bugs when hooks are in use.

questions.q: In a model with self.hidden = nn.Linear(10, 20), what does named_parameters() report for that layer's weight, and why?
options: 'weight', because submodule nesting is not reflected in names
'hidden.weight', because the name reflects that weight belongs to the submodule stored at self.hidden
'linear_weight_0', an auto-generated index
Nothing, because nn.Linear parameters aren't tracked automatically
questions.explain: nn.Module tracks submodules and nests their parameter names with a dot, reflecting the attribute path — here 'hidden.weight' for the weight belonging to the nn.Linear stored at self.hidden.

questions.q: How does nn.Module discover which attributes are parameters, enabling model.parameters() to work automatically?
options: You must manually register each one by calling model.register(name, tensor)
It scans a global list defined outside the class
It automatically inspects its own attributes (recursively through any submodules) for nn.Parameter instances and nn.Module instances at assignment time
It only finds parameters defined inside forward()
questions.explain: nn.Module overrides attribute assignment (__setattr__) to detect when an nn.Parameter or nn.Module is being assigned, automatically registering it so later calls to .parameters() or .named_parameters() find it, including recursively through nested submodules.
